spec_match.rationale: Targets the CSSWG serialization resolution exactly — both spellings read back as flow-* once shipped — via live specified and computed CSSOM round-trips.

interactive.rationale: The round-trip table is generated from real setProperty/readback cycles with a re-run button, and the audit button evaluates real equality checks against the browser's actual serialization.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the round-trip table and a breakage audit; both are on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Distinguishes three regimes honestly — pre-157, parse-without-serialization (flags split), and full aliasing — and shows the migrated includes() pattern passing on all of them.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5069051687731200 and PR 14539 which carries the serialization resolution.

conformance.rationale: The suite pins both halves separately (specified and computed serialization) plus the retention round-trip, matching this page's table.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): flex-start/flex-end read back as written (legacy regime), flow-* dropped with computed falling back to 'normal', audit reported all four checks OK with the explanation that BREAKS lines appear under the new regime; re-run rebuilt the six rows; zero console errors; both viewports clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the round-trip ran with the detected regime and the audit outcome with its break count.

design_system.rationale: Token colours (92400e legacy / 064e3b new / 7f1d1d dropped verdicts, all AA+ on their backgrounds), 44px buttons, no static card — the snippet is backed by the live table above it.

accessibility.rationale: Table has a caption and scopes, verdicts are text not colour alone, buttons are native, the audit output is a role=status aria-live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800: table wraps via overflow-wrap, zero document overflow, identical results.

openQuestions.title: Verify the mixed regime when the two flags split
openQuestions.detail: CSSFlowStartAndEndSerialization depends_on CSSFlowStartAndEnd, so a build with only the parse flag enabled should hit this page's 'mixed state' branch (flow-* parses, flex-* still serializes as written). When a 157+ binary is available, verify that branch and the full-aliasing branch, and confirm the audit's BREAKS lines appear exactly for the two legacy comparisons.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detect CSS value support graceful fallback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Detect regimes from observed behaviour, not version strings, and give migration guidance that works across the transition.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The regime banner derives purely from the measured round-trip (never the UA string), and the recommended includes()/CSS.supports patterns are demonstrated passing on the current regime by the audit.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel toggle buttons no horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep data tables readable on narrow screens with wrapping cell content.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All table cells use overflow-wrap:anywhere; verified 0px overflow at 360px.

summary: The migration hazard made concrete: a live CSSOM round-trip table showing Chromium 141's legacy regime (flex-* reads back as written, flow-* dropped) and a runnable audit demonstrating which equality checks the flow-* serialization will break, with the safe patterns proven in place. Cloud headless verification, both viewports clean.
